top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a specific, original and mature advance: magic-wavelength trapping lets many neutral atoms be interrogated on a narrow transition without Doppler or recoil shifts, bringing accuracy and stability to the 10^-18 level, reproduced across laboratories and used in geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The Katori-Ye allocation and a citation focused on many-atom lattice interrogation handle the overlap with earlier clock and comb prizes; residual credit questions (Takamoto, Hong, Ludlow, Lemke, NIST/PTB/SYRTE groups) do not outweigh the case, so awarding is preferable to no award.
